calls.call_name: Discovery Call: Qualifying the lead and mapping their current ERP stack (Duration: 25 mins).
calls.transcript:
Sales Rep (Alex): Hi Jordan, thanks for joining me. I know we booked 25 minutes, does that still work for you?

Prospect (Jordan): Yeah, hi Alex. I’ve got a hard stop at the bottom of the hour, but 25 minutes is fine. I saw your emails about, uh, the static forecasting stuff.

Sales Rep (Alex): Great. Yeah, I wanted to dig into that a bit. I noticed Summit Peak had a massive holiday season last year, but I read a press release about some fulfillment delays. What’s the reality on the ground regarding your inventory levels right now?

Prospect (Jordan): To be honest, it’s... it's a bit of a rollercoaster. Like you mentioned in your note, we were stocking out of our best-selling hiking gear in July, which killed us on revenue. And now? Now we’re sitting on pallets of camping accessories that aren't moving because the season shifted. It's frustrating.

Sales Rep (Alex): That sounds painful. It’s the classic bullwhip effect. How are you currently trying to predict these swings? What’s the stack look like?

Prospect (Jordan): Currently? It’s brute force. We pull data out of our ERP and dump it into Excel. My team of four analysts spends about, I don't know, 15 hours a week just cleaning rows before we even run a pivot table. It’s all manual.

Sales Rep (Alex): Wow, 15 hours a week per person or total? And which ERP are you on?

Prospect (Jordan): Total, mostly. And we’re on NetSuite. We moved to NetSuite two years ago, but the native forecasting module just... it was too generic. So we went back to spreadsheets.

Sales Rep (Alex): Got it. So, NetSuite is the source of truth, but Excel is the execution layer. That’s actually a perfect fit for us; OmniFlow sits right on top of NetSuite. We pull that historical data automatically so your team stops cleaning rows. 

Prospect (Jordan): That sounds nice, theoretically. But look, the last time we touched our tech stack, it was a nightmare. We had downtime for three days.

Sales Rep (Alex): I hear you. That’s a huge concern. Who else would be involved in the decision to bring in a tool like ours? I assume you’d need sign-off?

Prospect (Jordan): Yeah, definitely. I run Supply Chain, but Marcus, our CFO, holds the purse strings. He’s... well, he’s pretty old school. He likes Excel because it feels 'free' to him. He’s going to ask about the upfront cost and, more importantly, he’s terrified of disruption. If I tell him we need to integrate new AI software, he’s gonna think 'implementation hell.'

Sales Rep (Alex): Understood. Marcus is focused on risk mitigation and CAPEX. If we can show him that our implementation is essentially a plug-and-play connector with NetSuite—zero downtime—and that the ROI comes from reducing those carrying costs you mentioned on the camping gear, do you think he'd listen?

Prospect (Jordan): Maybe. If the numbers are real. We need to sort this out before the holiday rush starts in November. If we go into Q4 blind again, heads might roll.

Sales Rep (Alex): Okay. Let's do this. I want to set up a technical demo specifically to show the NetSuite connector so you can see how lightweight it is. Then we can build a business case for Marcus. How does Thursday look?

Prospect (Jordan): Thursday works. Send the invite.
calls.summary: Conducted a discovery call with Jordan (Supply Chain Lead) at Summit Peak. Confirmed the pain points hypothesized in the outreach: they are suffering from significant stockouts during peak seasons and holding excess inventory during off-seasons. The current process involves exporting data from NetSuite into Excel, which requires heavy manual cleaning by a team of four analysts. Jordan is interested in a solution but identified the CFO, Marcus, as a major blocker. Marcus prefers legacy methods (Excel) due to perceived low cost and has a strong fear of operational disruption during implementation. Agreed to schedule a technical demo focused on the NetSuite integration to prove ease of deployment before engaging the CFO.

calls.call_name: Product Demo: Showcasing the 'One-Click Import' feature and ROI dashboard to proving value (Duration: 45 mins).
calls.transcript:
Sales Rep (Alex): Hey Jordan, thanks for hopping on again. I know things are probably getting hectic with Q3 ramping up. How’s the team holding up?

Prospect (Jordan): Hey Alex. Yeah, 'hectic' is... uh, putting it mildly. We just spent the last 48 hours trying to reconcile the July inventory against the actuals in NetSuite, and, well, Excel crashed on us twice. So, the timing is good.

Sales Rep (Alex): That sounds painful, but exactly why we’re here. I want to be respectful of the 45 minutes we have. The goal today is twofold: First, I want to show you that 'One-Click Import' we talked about to prove to Marcus that this won’t shut down your ops for a week. Second, I want to show you the ROI dashboard so you have the ammo to justify the spend. Does that still sound right?

Prospect (Jordan): Spot on. Honestly, if you can show me it doesn't take a PhD to integrate, that’s half the battle. Marcus is convinced any new software means two weeks of downtime. He’s got serious PTSD from our ERP migration three years ago.

Sales Rep (Alex): Understood. Let me share my screen. Can you see the OmniFlow dashboard?

Prospect (Jordan): Yep, got it.

Sales Rep (Alex): Okay. So, you mentioned you’re on NetSuite, right? Look at the top right corner here. This is our 'Integrations Hub'. I’m going to select NetSuite. Now, usually, this is where people expect to see a bunch of code. But watch this. I click 'Connect via SuiteTalk', enter the API token—which your IT team generates in about five minutes—and hit 'Sync'.

Prospect (Jordan): Okay... wait, is that live data pulling in right now?

Sales Rep (Alex): That is live. See the progress bar? It’s mapping your SKUs, historical sales data from the last 24 months, and current stock levels. It’s done. That took, what, 30 seconds?

Prospect (Jordan): Wow. Okay. That... that actually pulled the SKU categories correctly too? usually, the formatting gets messed up because we use alphanumeric codes.

Sales Rep (Alex): It uses AI to detect the schema. So, no manual column mapping. The system is ready to forecast immediately. No downtime, no operational pause. Your team keeps selling while this runs in the background.

Prospect (Jordan): That’s... honestly, that’s better than I expected. I can definitely sell that to Marcus. He thinks we need to hire consultants to set this up.

Sales Rep (Alex): No consultants needed. Now, let’s look at the second piece—the money. I’ve loaded some anonymized data similar to Summit Peak’s volume to show you the ROI Dashboard. You mentioned last time that you guys are bleeding on carrying costs during the off-season?

Prospect (Jordan): Yeah. Last year we wrote off... I think it was around $215,000 in unsold inventory just from Q4 leftovers. It sits in the warehouse, costing us storage, and then we liquidate it for pennies.

Sales Rep (Alex): Okay, $215k is a significant number. Look at this 'Carrying Cost Reduction' widget. Based on your volume, OmniFlow identifies slow-moving SKUs 6 weeks earlier than a spreadsheet trendline would. Conservatively, if we reduce that overstock by just 20%, that’s $43,000 saved in year one just on write-offs alone. That doesn't even count the revenue gain from avoiding stockouts in peak season.

Prospect (Jordan): Right. And stockouts are the other headache. We missed about $150k in revenue last December because we ran out of our top-selling parkas.

Sales Rep (Alex): Exactly. So, combined, you're looking at a $365k problem annually. Our enterprise tier is a fraction of that. This dashboard updates daily, so Marcus can literally see the 'Cash Saved' metric ticking up.

Prospect (Jordan): That’s the screen I need to show him. He loves a good efficiency graph. 

Sales Rep (Alex): We can generate a custom report for him. Speaking of which, if we wanted to get this in place to save that Q4 revenue this year, what kind of timeline are we looking at?

Prospect (Jordan): We need to be live before the holiday rush kicks in. Ideally, I want this running by October 1st. Is that realistic?

Sales Rep (Alex): Since integration takes minutes, yes. We’d just need a week for team training. If we sign by mid-September, October 1st is easy.

Prospect (Jordan): Okay. The biggest hurdle left is the budget. Marcus has a hard cap of $75,000 for 'Operational Efficiency Tools' for the fiscal year. Where do we land?

Sales Rep (Alex): For the volume you’re doing, the license plus the premium support package comes in at $68,000 annually. So we are under that cap.

Prospect (Jordan): Perfect. That’s... yeah, that’s really good news. Okay, send me the recording of this integration demo. I’m going to put time on Marcus’s calendar for next Tuesday. I think I can get him on board now.

Sales Rep (Alex): Awesome. I’ll send that over along with a one-pager on the ROI analysis we just discussed. Good luck with the reconciling today!

Prospect (Jordan): Thanks, Alex. Talk soon.
calls.summary: Demonstrated the OmniFlow platform to Jordan, specifically focusing on the NetSuite API integration to address the CFO's fear of operational disruption. Jordan validated that the 'One-Click Import' was significantly faster than their current manual process. Pivoted to the ROI dashboard, using Jordan's figures ($215k in write-offs and $150k in lost revenue) to build a business case. Confirmed the pricing ($68k) fits within the CFO's $75k allocated budget. Agreed on a target go-live date of October 1st to catch the holiday season. Jordan is now equipped to bring Marcus (CFO) to the table for final approval.
